12.0.0.en: 1 "Ephraim feedeth on wind, and followeth after the east wind: he daily increaseth lies and extortion; and they do make a covenant with the Assyrians, and oil is carried into Egypt. 2 The LORD hath also a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways; according to his doings will he recompense him.

12.0.1.en: In bitter rebuke He says: "Ephraim feedeth on wind, and followeth after the east wind: he daily increaseth lies and extortion; and they do make a covenant with the Assyrians, and oil is carried into Egypt" [1].

12.0.2.en: Ephraim forsook his good Shepherd, the giver of true good things, and went out to tend the wind, to acquire nothing. Poor Ephraim, for he toils in tending a wind without benefit... and would that it were any wind, but it is "the east wind." As St. Hippolytus of Rome says, the east wind signifies "the Antichrist," who appears in the East, opposing the Lord Christ in His Church: [What is the burning wind coming from the east but the Antichrist, who shatters and dries up the water-courses and the fruit of the trees in his days (Hos 13:15), since men set their hearts upon his works? He shatters them because of the truth, and they in their hardness serve him]. Thus Ephraim turned from the kingdom of Christ to the Antichrist, and bore the marks of his master: "lies and extortion and making covenants with the world instead of God..."

12.1.s.en: 2. The need for earnestness in returning to Him

12.1.0.en: 3 "In the womb he took his brother by the heel, and in his strength he strove with God. 4 He strove with the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him: he found him in Bethel, and there he spake with us; 5 even the LORD God of hosts, Jehovah is his name. 6 And thou, return to thy God: keep mercy and truth, and wait on thy God continually.

12.1.1.en: Since the people take pride in their father "Jacob," He presented him to them as an example of striving with men and with God, who obtained by his striving the meeting with God, who loves those who strive. "In the womb he took his brother by the heel" [3]; while still in his mother's womb, not yet come out into the world, he was striving, and he took hold of his brother's heel to draw him back, seizing from him the birthright and the blessing.

12.1.2.en: "And in his strength he strove with God, he strove with the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him" [3-4].. He represents a wonderful example of striving with God, for he gave all his energy to striving with God, who wrestled with him until the dawn to teach him striving and the spirit of victory. And when Jacob realized that the victory was a gift from God and not by his arms, he "wept," and God had mercy on him, revealing Himself to him: "he found him in Bethel, and there he spake with us; even the LORD God of hosts, Jehovah is his name" [4-5].

12.2.0.en: 7 "He is like a Canaanite, the balances of deceit are in his hand: he loveth to oppress. 8 And Ephraim said, Yet I am become rich, I have found me out substance: in all my labours they shall find none iniquity in me that were sin. 9 And I that am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt will yet make thee to dwell in tabernacles, as in the days of the solemn feast. 10 I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets. 11 Surely they in Gilead have become iniquity, nothing but vanity: in Gilgal they sacrificed bullocks, and their altars are as heaps in the furrows of the field."

12.2.1.en: The people did not bear the spirit of discernment by which the true Shepherd, the giver of good things, is known from the deceiving shepherds; therefore the Lord requires of them to abandon these standards, contemplating God's true care.

12.2.2.en: "He is like a Canaanite, the balances of deceit are in his hand: he loveth to oppress" [7]. He lost his nature as a son of God and became like a Gentile without wisdom, a lover of injustice, who slanders God, and even himself. The sign of his deceitful balances is that he thought himself rich and in no need of God: "And Ephraim said, Yet I am become rich, I have found me out substance: in all my labours they shall find none iniquity in me that were sin" [8]. He forgot that God is the one who released him from bondage, sent him the prophets, spoke with him in every way, and trains him: "And I that am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt will yet make thee to dwell in tabernacles, as in the days of the solemn feast. I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets" [10].

12.3.0.en: 12 And Jacob fled into the wilderness of Aram, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep. 13 And by a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, and by a prophet was he preserved. 14 Ephraim provoked him to anger most bitterly: therefore shall he leave his blood upon him, and his reproach shall his Lord return unto him.

12.3.1.en: If Jacob their father spent long years in the wilderness of Aram, serving and tending sheep for a wife, is it not fitting for his children to serve in the wilderness of this world for the sake of their Shepherd, the Bridegroom of their souls? He says: "And Jacob fled into the wilderness of Aram, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep" [12].

13.0.0.en: 1 When Ephraim spake trembling, he exalted himself in Israel; but when he offended in Baal, he died. 2 And now they sin more and more, and have made them molten images of their silver, and idols according to their own understanding, all of it the work of the craftsmen: of them they say, The sacrificers of men kiss the calves. 3 Therefore they shall be as the morning cloud and as the early dew that passeth away, as the chaff that is driven with the whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney.

13.0.1.en: In order to present Himself as a King who saves their souls, He reveals to them what sin, especially the worship of Baal, has done to them, saying: "When Ephraim spake trembling, he exalted himself in Israel; but when he offended in Baal, he died" [1].

13.0.2.en: When Ephraim walked as his father Jacob walked, in the holy fear of God, he became exalted among the tribes and his standing became prominent, and all were in awe before him. So also those who humble themselves before God, He exalts. But when Ephraim attached himself to Baal in sin, he lost not only his reputation and his awe-inspiring dignity but he "died"... and so he became in need of a mighty Savior able to raise him from the dead.

13.1.0.en: The strange thing is that sin, with the death it carries, draws man's heart not to remorse over what he has reached, but draws him all the more from sin to sin: "And now they sin more and more" [2]. This causes them to lose the work of God's word in them, since it is "molten images of their silver" [2]; they make it according to their skill or understanding, that is, they set up their gods according to their own whims and do not submit to the mind of God.

13.1.1.en: They set up idols to worship: "of them they say, The sacrificers of men kiss the calves" [2]. Perhaps he means that because of these idols they tell the priests, who in truth slaughter men by their corruption and uncleanness, to offer on their behalf the most precious of the animals, "the calves," as sacrifices to Baal... For the priests are wicked, and the sacrifices, whatever their value, are an abomination.

13.2.0.en: He describes those who walk thus, apostate from God their Savior, as those who "shall be as the morning cloud and as the early dew that passeth away, as the chaff that is driven with the whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney" [3]. These appear like a cloud that heralds the coming down of rain (a sign of God's grace), but it is the deceptive morning cloud, which as soon as the sun rises disappears altogether. They are like the early dew that quickly vanishes without watering the earth. They are also the light, trivial chaff that is cast about on every side, and like smoke from the chimney (the flue) they quickly disperse and vanish (Ps 68:2).

13.3.0.en: 4 "Yet I am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt, and thou shalt know no god but me: for there is no saviour beside me. 5 I did know thee in the wilderness, in the land of thirst. 6 When they fed, they were filled; they were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore have they forgotten me. 7 Therefore I will be unto them as a lion: as a leopard by the way will I lie in wait for them. 8 I will meet them as a bear that is bereaved of her whelps, and will rend the caul of their heart, and there will I devour them like a lioness: the wild beast of the wilderness shall tear them.

13.3.1.en: Wanting to affirm His saving work for them, He gave them a practical lesson from the life of their fathers, when He delivered them from their bondage to Pharaoh and tended them in the midst of the wilderness until they were satisfied: "Yet I am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt, and thou shalt know no god but me: for there is no saviour beside me. I did know thee in the wilderness, in the land of thirst. When they fed, they were filled" [4-6]. He satisfied them in the land of thirst when they were in great distress. But when they were satisfied from His hands they denied Him: "they were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore have they forgotten me" [6].

13.3.2.en: When the body is satisfied it forgets God its Creator and is lifted up in pride, as it is said in the book of Deuteronomy: "But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation" (Deut 32:15).

13.4.0.en: Before this denial God stood before them firmly: "Therefore I will be unto them as a lion: as a leopard by the way will I lie in wait for them. I will meet them as a bear that is bereaved of her whelps, and will rend the caul of their heart, and there will I devour them like a lioness: the wild beast of the wilderness shall tear them" [7-8]. As the prophet Isaiah says: "But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them" (Isa 63:10). By this description He revealed the bitterness of God's soul toward His denying children, so that He became to them as an enemy fighting them violently like a lion, watching their movements like a leopard, violently like a bereaved bear, sending upon them chastisements that devour and eat them like a lioness... All this is because they became vessels of wrath fitted to destruction (Rom 9:22).

13.5.s.en: 3. Their rejection of the saving King

13.5.0.en: 9 "Thy destruction, O Israel, is that thou art against me, against thy help. 10 Where now is thy king, that he may save thee in all thy cities? and thy judges, of whom thou saidst, Give me a king and princes? 11 I gave thee a king in mine anger, and took him away in my wrath. 12 The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored up. 13 The sorrows of a travailing woman shall come upon him: he is an unwise son; for he should not stay long in the place of the breaking forth of children.

13.5.1.en: "Thy destruction, O Israel, is that thou art against me, against thy help" [9]. According to the translation of the Jesuits, "Destruction is from thee, O Israel, but thy help is in me." What befalls Israel springs from its destructive behavior, which leads it to death, while its salvation is in the rejected King, God their God, whom they forgot, asking for themselves a king after their own desire, as He says to them: "Where now is thy king, that he may save thee in all thy cities? and thy judges, of whom thou saidst, Give me a king and princes? I gave thee a king in mine anger, and took him away in my wrath" [9-11].

13.5.2.en: Perhaps by this He refers to them when they desired to have a king to judge them like all the nations (1 Sam 8:5), which grieved the heart of Samuel the prophet. Nevertheless God gave them Saul as king according to the desire of their heart, and in His wrath took him from them because of his evils. For our discipline God allows us to obtain what we desire, so that we may realize our need to accept God's will rather than carry out our own will.

13.6.0.en: They obtained the desire of their heart, a "king" according to their wish, and their iniquity increased: "The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored up. The sorrows of a travailing woman shall come upon him: he is an unwise son; for he should not stay long in the place of the breaking forth of children" [12-13]. They "treasure up unto themselves wrath against the day of wrath" (Rom 2:5), and so they destroy themselves. Their sins are bound up for their account; God does not forget them, and they are stored in a safe place so that they may give account for them... They thought they were hidden, that no one sees them, that they are forgotten with time, and did not realize that, since they do not remember them seeking forgiveness, they are kept for their destruction. They have become like the woman who carries a child within her, for the labor with its pains is surely coming. But Ephraim, unwisely, fled from contemplating or thinking about the pain that happens because of sin, so as to know the cause of the pain and be delivered from it by God his Savior.

13.7.0.en: 14 "I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, where are thy plagues? O grave, where is thy sting? repentance shall be hid from mine eyes."

13.7.1.en: He who redeemed their fathers from the bondage of Pharaoh is able alone to redeem them even from death and to deliver them from the grave: "I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, where are thy plagues? O grave, where is thy sting? repentance shall be hid from mine eyes" [14].

13.7.2.en: He accomplishes for them what no other king can accomplish for them, for He not only releases them from captivity but has authority to bring them out of the grave and deliver them from death, which was fulfilled by the Savior's entering into death to destroy its authority. As St. Jerome says: [We have this consolation, that the Word of God has slain death... (Our Lord Jesus) died in order that by His death He might put death itself to death.] He also speaks to death, saying: [You have swallowed our Jonah (our Christ), but He is alive even in your belly. You carried Him as dead so that the storm of the world might be calmed and our Nineveh be saved by preaching Him. Yes, He has defeated you and slain you... By His death you have become dead, and by His death we have become alive. You swallowed Him, and behold, you are swallowed up. While you were stricken with desire for the body which He took, seizing it as prey with the claws of your greed, behold, you are wounded within...!.]

13.7.3.en: This is God's promise to us... He gave us authority over death, without repentance or change in His promise, for He says: "repentance shall be hid from mine eyes," that is, I do not retract what I have promised.

13.8.0.en: 15 "Though he be fruitful among his brethren, an east wind shall come, the wind of the LORD shall come up from the wilderness, and his spring shall become dry, and his fountain shall be dried up: he shall spoil the treasure of all pleasant vessels. 16 Samaria shall be recompensed; for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword: their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up."

13.8.1.en: If the Lord Christ by His death gives life, slaying death, then by divine permission the Antichrist comes and blows as an east wind to dry up within man the spring of the Holy Spirit and make his inner fountain dry and cause him to lose all his fruit: "Though he be fruitful among his brethren, an east wind shall come, the wind of the LORD shall come up from the wilderness, and his spring shall become dry, and his fountain shall be dried up: he shall spoil the treasure of all pleasant vessels. Samaria shall be recompensed; for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword: their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up" [15-16]. This speech was fulfilled literally by the blowing of the Assyrian captivity from the east, which destroyed Israel entirely and its capital Samaria, and it will be fulfilled at the end of the ages when the wind of the "Antichrist" blows coming from the east, and it is called "the wind of the LORD" because it is by His permission.
